derivation: Field set is EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2. Sources are SOURCE_AUTHORITY_PACK sections E, F, G, H and I only.

The least standardised category in the library. Section I of the pack records that scheduling, rostering and resource optimisation have no standard anywhere and that ISO 30409:2016 is STRATEGIC workforce planning which must not be stretched to cover them. Nine of eighteen processes rest on judgment and say so.

Qualification is the part that is real, and it is asymmetric. 49 CFR 192 Subpart N gives gas a written programme, identified covered tasks and evaluated individuals. Electric distribution has no federal qualification programme requirement at all - 29 CFR 1910.269(a)(2) defines a qualified employee and 1926 Subpart P a competent person, and neither is a programme. 14.2.5 and 14.2.6 are gas only for that reason.
49 CFR Part 199 drug and alcohol testing is gas only and reaches this category because a positive result or refusal removes a person from availability at 14.1.3.

Five cross-references already merged in 3.0 and 16.0 bind this category and all five hold: 14.1.2 as the organisational master, 14.1.3 owning the live person status record, 14.2.4 restricting assignment on a lapsed qualification, 14.2.5 qualifying operator people only, and 14.4.1 owning pay rules that 3.2 consumes and must not invent.
taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.
gaps: No standard defines a worker master, an organisational structure master, availability status, access provisioning, competency profiles, time capture, crew cascade, timesheet approval, pay rules, payroll interfacing or time reconciliation for utility work. Every one of those is recorded as judgment rather than attributed to a source that does not reach it.
49 CFR 192.805(g) sets no requalification interval - it is entirely operator-set - so 14.2.2 records the operator's own figure and its source.
49 CFR 192.805 requires direction and observation of an unqualified individual and sets NO span-of-control number. 14.2.6 records the limit as the operator's and never cites it to the section.
Offline mobile behaviour, sync conflict resolution and field data capture are entirely vendor-defined, which is why 14.3.1 specifies what is captured and not how the device behaves.

processes.name: Review, approve and exception-handle time
processes.intent: Approve the time, and deal with what does not look right before pay does.
activities: Take the submitted timesheets for the approval group
Test each against the exceptions the operator defined
Approve, query or reject, recording which and why
Release approved time to costing and to pay

trigger.text: Submitted timesheets are due for approval.

inputs.what: Approval authority from the org structure

outputs.what: Approved time released to costing and pay
Queried or rejected time with its reason

systems.service: approved time for cost and pay
approved hours against the work order

controls.text: Approval authority derives from 14.1.2's reporting structure. An approver outside the line is the most common audit finding in time administration and it is a structure problem, not a workflow one.
The exception rules are the operator's. No standard defines what an anomalous timesheet looks like, so the rules and their thresholds are recorded as the operator's and reviewed as such.
Approval is the gate before cost and pay diverge. The same approved hours go to 5.2.1 as work cost and to 14.4.3 as pay, and approving them separately is how the two stop reconciling.

processes.name: Apply pay rules, premiums and agreements

group.name: Cost labour and interface to payroll

processes.intent: Hold the pay rules, premiums and agreement terms the hours are valued at.
activities: Hold the agreement terms, rates, premiums and their trigger conditions
Apply them to the approved hours to produce a valued entry
Maintain the terms as agreements are renegotiated, with effective dates
Publish the constraints that scheduling must plan within

trigger.text: Approved hours require valuing, or an agreement term changes.

inputs.what: Approved hours with their time types
Agreement terms, rates and premium triggers
Effective dates for a changed term

outputs.what: Valued hours with the rule that valued them
Labour-agreement constraints for scheduling

controls.text: This OWNS pay rules, premiums and overtime. 3.2 consumes the constraints and must not invent them; a second rule set in scheduling will eventually pay differently.
Every valued entry records the rule that valued it. A premium without its trigger cannot be re-derived when the agreement changes, leaving back-pay with no basis.
Terms change on effective dates and hours are valued at the rule in force when worked. Applying today's rate to last period's hours is the costliest error here.

processes.name: Post labour cost to work and project

group.name: Cost labour and interface to payroll

processes.intent: Put the cost of the hours onto the work they were spent on.
activities: Take the valued hours and the work order they were recorded against
Post the labour cost to the work order and to the project above it
Split the posting where the hours crossed work orders or cost objects
Return exceptions where the hours will not post

trigger.text: Valued hours are ready to be posted to work.

inputs.what: Valued hours and their work order
Work order and project cost structure
Cost object rules for the posting

outputs.what: Labour cost posted to work and project
Posting exceptions for resolution

controls.text: 5.2.1 posts labour actuals as part of closing work; this posts them as part of paying people. They are the same hours reaching the same work order from two directions, and they must reconcile or the work cost is wrong in one of them.
A posting that fails is an exception, not a silent loss. Hours that will not post because the work order is closed still have to land somewhere, and 14.4.4 is where that is resolved.
Hours crossing work orders split at the posting, not at capture. Making the worker split them in the field produces a division that nobody can audit against what actually happened.

processes.name: Transfer approved time to payroll

group.name: Cost labour and interface to payroll

processes.intent: Hand the approved time to payroll, once, and know that it arrived.
activities: Take the approved time for the pay period at the cut-off
Transfer it to payroll in the form the payroll system requires
Capture the acknowledgement and reconcile the transferred totals
Hold anything the cut-off excluded for the following period

trigger.text: The payroll cut-off for the period is reached.

inputs.what: Approved time for the pay period
Transfer format the payroll system requires

outputs.what: Transferred time and its acknowledgement
Time held for the following period

systems.service: the interface itself and its exceptions

controls.text: The transfer happens once per period. A re-sent period pays twice, and the acknowledgement is what proves it was sent and received rather than sent twice or not at all.
Time that misses the cut-off is HELD, not dropped. It belongs to the following period with its original dates intact, and losing the original dates is what breaks the reconciliation at 14.4.4.
15.5 owns the integration mechanics. This process owns what is transferred and whether it arrived; how the interface is built and monitored is not specified here.

processes.name: Reconcile time and pay exceptions

group.name: Cost labour and interface to payroll

processes.intent: Make the hours worked, the hours costed and the hours paid agree.
activities: Compare hours approved, hours posted to work and hours paid for the period
Identify the differences and establish what caused each
Correct the side that is wrong, through the route that side allows
Return the residual and the reason it could not be resolved

trigger.text: A pay period has closed and requires reconciliation.

outputs.what: Reconciled position across the three
Corrections routed to the side at fault
Residual difference with its reason

systems.service: reconciliation across time, cost and pay

controls.text: Three populations must agree: hours approved at 14.3.4, posted at 14.4.2 and 5.2.1, and paid at 14.4.3. Reconciling two leaves the third to drift, usually the work cost.
A correction takes the route its side allows. Time already paid is adjusted in the following period; 14.3.3 must never look as though it can undo a payment.
An unresolved residual is recorded with its reason, not written off. One repeating each period is a systematic defect, and only visible if it is kept.

measures.name: Reconciliation completeness
measures.definition: Proportion of periods reconciled across all three populations.

Difference between paid and posted to work
